note: MUTATION RESTORE: how you put the file back decides whether cargo rebuilds, and the tidiest method is the one that hides. Restoring a mutated source with  preserves the backup ORIGINAL mtime, which is older than the build you did in between, so cargo judges the crate fresh and rebuilds nothing. Every later command then runs the MUTATED binary against a restored source. Measured today on campaign/the-tidemark: clippy, make gate-commit rc=0, and a post-commit confirmation run all executed the mutated binary while  was clean and grep showed the restored constant. Three independent confirmations, all correct about the source, all describing a binary that no longer matched it. SAFE vs UNSAFE restores: an editor write and  stamp mtime to NOW, so cargo rebuilds -- safe.  preserves the old stamp -- unsafe.  likewise. Plain  stamps now -- safe.  after any restore closes it, costs nothing, leaves the tree clean. THE TELL, and it generalises past mutation work: the only signal was inside the panic text of a run -- a count the current source could not produce. Every instrument we point at a tree describes the SOURCE; the binary is visible only in what it says while running. So verify a restore with OUTPUT that carries a value only the restored source can yield, never with an exit code -- rc cannot distinguish the two worlds, a printed constant can. THE REVIEWING HALF: a report of applied the mutation, confirmed RED, restored, clean tree is NOT a verification. Clean tree proved nothing; the pass does, and only if its output names a discriminating value. Found by campaign/the-tidemark while proving a power gate could arm; the safe-restore row and the printed-discriminator rule corroborated by campaign/the-trencher, which had reached both by habit rather than by knowing the hazard.
